Subject: Re: Incident - 2027-05-31 latency & 503 spike

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the quick sync this morning. The attached timeline and metrics you shared offline are helpful. Two asks from Aurora ops: (1) a short, shareable one-paragraph RCA we can distribute in our platform status channel for customers; (2) a clear set of compensatory/operational commitments (what you will ship, when) so our procurement and legal teams can close the loop on the SLA review.

We're still seeing elevated tail latency for long-sequence generation on a small subset of requests (0.5% of traffic) — if you have a mitigation plan that reduces customer-facing impact in the next 48 hours, that would go a long way.

— Sara

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@aurora.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Aurora: operational remedy sprint, RCA delivery & account commitments

Sara — thanks for the note and for flagging the tail-latency detail. Per our postmortem work this morning I’m sharing the draft RCA (attached) plus the short-form summary below for your status channel.

One-paragraph summary for external customers (ready to copy):
"On 2027-05-31 at approximately 14:04 UTC, a hardware-side scheduling regression on a minority of inference hosts led to prolonged context-switching and degraded KV-cache performance for long-sequence workloads. This caused elevated tail latency and an increase in HTTP 503 responses for affected sessions. We deployed a targeted kernel-level scheduler patch and a temporary routing rule the same day; both mitigations reduced customer impact. We will complete a staged rollout of a longer-term fix (quantized cache alignment and improved backpressure) by 2027-06-14 and provide daily status updates until the work is complete."

Immediate commitments (48h window):
- Deploy additional routing rule to shift long-sequence traffic to healthy pool (in place within 3h) — DONE 2027-06-02 02:30 UTC
- Enable adaptive KV-cache eviction threshold for affected model families (temporary knob) — DONE 2027-06-02 05:10 UTC
- Provide Aurora with a temporary throughput cap for their non-critical batch jobs to alleviate queuing (by 2027-06-03) — scheduled

Planned corrective work (production rollout by 2027-06-14):
- Kernel scheduler patch (longer-term) with regression tests and perf guardrails
- Quantized cache alignment to prevent re-entrancy under heavy KV load
- Improved load-shedding policy for long-running sessions

I’ve attached the full draft RCA and timeline. Internal action owners are in the remediation checklist — Marcus will lead the kernel patch, Neha will lead customer comms and credits, Kimberly will track QA and rollout gating.

Next steps:
1) Confirm the short paragraph is acceptable for Aurora status channel.
2) We will circulate a remediation cadence (daily updates) and a JIRA ticket with acceptance criteria by EOD.

Jordan

Attachments: aurora_rca_draft.pdf; timeline_events.csv

Team — looping in the leadership and SRE owners for the commitment plan. Draft exec summary for internal leadership + credit/contract coordination with Finance:

Executive summary (internal):
- Incident: 2027-05-31 latency + 503s caused by scheduler regression impacting ~0.5% Aurora traffic (long-sequence workloads).
- Impact: Customer-facing slowdowns and intermittent errors; revenue exposure modest but reputational risk high for Aurora (enterprise).
- Immediate mitigations completed: routing rule, KV eviction knob. Residual tail latency remains for a small slice.
- Remediation: Kernel patch + cache alignment due 2027-06-14 with QA stretch through 2027-06-21.
- Ask: leadership approval for a one-time goodwill credit (recommendation: 20% of May inference spend up to a cap), and approval to schedule a 30-min executive briefing with Aurora's CTO next week.

Action tracker (owner — eta — status):
- Customer-facing RCA paragraph — Neha — 2027-06-02 — sent to Aurora (awaiting signoff)
- Kernel scheduler patch — Marcus Lin — 2027-06-14 — in progress
- Rollout QA & perf gates — Kimberly Park — 2027-06-21 — planned
- Goodwill credit proposal & legal review — Jordan Blake / Finance — 2027-06-04 — pending approval
- Daily status email cadence to Aurora — Neha — 2027-06-02 onward — active

Please review recommended credit and the briefing timing — I’ll draft the executive slide for the CTO meeting once we have signoff on credits.

-Neha

Status update:
- Kernel scheduler patch merged to canary 2027-06-06 23:10 UTC; initial canary results show 92% reduction in tail latency for the affected workload slice.
- Rollout plan: canary -> regional pools -> global (expected complete 2027-06-14).
- QA gating: performance regressions flagged at 1% or higher will block global rollout; we have smoke tests and synthetic runs scheduled every 6 hours.

Action items for Aurora:
- Please confirm a 30-min window next week for an exec briefing with your CTO and head of platform — proposed slots: Tue 2027-06-08 10:00-10:30 PT or Wed 2027-06-09 14:00-14:30 PT.
- Confirm whether Aurora will accept the one-paragraph customer-facing summary (below) for posting to your status channel.

Customer-facing paragraph (same as draft):

This caused elevated tail latency and an increase in HTTP 503 responses for affected sessions. We deployed a targeted kernel-level scheduler patch and a temporary routing rule the same day; both mitigations reduced customer impact. We will complete a staged rollout of a longer-term fix (quantized cache alignment and improved backpressure) by 2027-06-14 and provide daily status updates until the work is complete."

Credits / commercial: we have a credit proposal drafted and are awaiting finance/legal signoff — I will share the exact figure by EOD 2027-06-08.

If you prefer a 15-min pre-brief before the exec call, Marcus and I can join.

Thanks — talk soon,
